summary: The game's skills, stats and perks, and the server's rules for what players earn by playing. Each XP gain in a player's game is requested from the server and granted under these rules, and progress the server never allowed is caught and fires playerProgressionRejected. Tracks are the stats strength, agility, vitality and speech, and skills such as stealth, horse_riding, fencing, thievery, alchemy, craftsmanship, drinking, survival, weapon_sword, heavy_weapons, marksmanship, weapon_large, weapon_unarmed, scholarship, houndmaster and prestige. To give XP and perks to one player, use Player's members. A resource can add perks of its own to the perk tree with the game's perk table files (see the Custom perks guide); they then work with every perk member here and on Player.

tracks.summary: All tracks, as { name, kind, cap, induced }.
tracks.exampleLua:
for _, track in ipairs(kcds.players.Progression.tracks()) do
  print(tostring(track.name) .. " (" .. tostring(track.kind) .. "), cap " .. tostring(track.cap))
end

perkNamed.summary: A perk by name or GUID, as { name, id, uiName, track, level, parent, visibility, kinds, autolearnable }, or null.
perkNamed.exampleLua:
local perk = kcds.players.Progression.perkNamed("Against all odds")
if perk then
  print(tostring(perk.name) .. ": " .. tostring(perk.track) .. " level " .. tostring(perk.level))
end

perks.summary: The game's perks, and the perks of your resources' own perk tables (see the Custom perks guide).

params.filter: Optional: `track`, a track name or 'main' for the main level's perks, and `visibleOnly`.

perks.example: const fencingPerks = kcds.players.Progression.perks({ track: 'fencing', visibleOnly: true });
perks.exampleLua: local fencingPerks = kcds.players.Progression.perks({ track = "fencing", visibleOnly = true })
perks.exampleCs: var fencingPerks = Progression.Perks(new { track = "fencing", visibleOnly = true });

xpNeeded.summary: The total XP a track needs to reach a level from 0.
xpNeeded.example:
const cost = kcds.players.Progression.xpNeeded('weapon_sword', 10);
console.info(`level 10 sword costs ${cost} XP`);
xpNeeded.exampleLua:
local cost = kcds.players.Progression.xpNeeded("weapon_sword", 10)
print("level 10 sword costs " .. tostring(cost) .. " XP")
xpNeeded.exampleCs:
var cost = Progression.XpNeeded("weapon_sword", 10);
Log.Info($"level 10 sword costs {cost} XP");

gameXp.summary: Whether players earn XP by playing.

setGameXp.summary: Lets players earn XP by playing, or not, so that only the server's grants count.

setXpGain.summary: Scales the XP from play on a track, or all with '*'. It runs from 0 to 1000, where 1 is the game's rate.

setXpCap.summary: The most XP per minute from play on a track, or all with '*'. 0 means no limit.

setMaxLevel.summary: The highest level reachable by play on a track.

setPerkText.summary: Changes what every player's game calls a perk and how it describes it: its name, description and lore text in the perk tree and wherever the game names it. A field left out keeps its text, null gives the game's own back. Players who join later read the same texts. Returns true when a text changed. Throws a TypeError for an unknown perk, or a text that is empty, too long (name 128 bytes, description and lore 4096) or has control characters other than line breaks and tabs.

params.texts: `name`, `description`, `lore`: a text each, or null for the game's own.

setPerkText.exampleLua: kcds.players.Progression.setPerkText("Against all odds", { name = "Racek's legacy", description = "You fight on when others would fall." })
setPerkText.exampleCs: Progression.SetPerkText("Against all odds", new { name = "Racek's legacy", description = "You fight on when others would fall." });

lockPerks.summary: Makes perks impossible to get for all players.

xpPercent.summary: A track's XP rule as a percentage, where 100 is the game's rate.

setXpPercent.summary: Sets a track's XP rule as a percentage, where 100 is the game's rate.
